function.arguments: {"rationale": "FP32 ulp at output magnitude ~11.09 is ~9.5e-7, so several independent half-ulp roundings (fl(exp*ln2h), two grouped additions, final store rounding), plus the truncated split-log2 constants, can plausibly push the absolute error past 1e-6 at the largest legal inputs like x=65504.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "Every finite FP16 value strictly greater than -1 is legal, including 65504, and every output element must satisfy abs(actual[i]-log(1+x[i])) <= 1e-6 with a single verdict for the entire legal domain."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract requires abs(actual - log(1+x)) <= 1e-6 for every legal FP16 value including the largest finite value 65504, with one verdict for the whole domain.", "statement": "For large legal inputs such as x=65504 (output ~11.09, FP32 ulp ~9.5e-7), the accumulated FP32 roundings in the exponent*log2 high part plus grouped additions and final store push the absolute error above the 1e-6 tolerance at some legal FP16 value."}

function.arguments: {"rationale": "0.33333 vs 1/3 (error 3.3e-6 relative) and 0.142857 vs 1/7, plus the dropped z^9 and higher terms, leave an approximation residual that scales with z^5..z^9 and is maximized at the z extremes reached exactly at the halving split boundary and the top of [1,2).", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "No particular polynomial approximation or intermediate rounding is part of the target; approximations are permitted only if they satisfy the fixed 1e-6 absolute tolerance throughout the entire legal domain, which includes every finite FP16 x > -1."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract permits approximations only if the fixed 1e-6 absolute bound holds throughout the entire legal domain; FP16 values whose fl(1+x) lands just above 1.65 or just below 2 are legal inputs and exercise the widest z ranges of the truncated polynomial.", "statement": "The truncated odd polynomial with rounded coefficients (0.33333 vs 1/3, 0.142857 vs 1/7, dropped z^9+ terms) produces error exceeding 1e-6 at the widest z ranges, e.g. mantissa just above 1.65 unhalved (z ~ 0.246, i.e. u ~ 1.65, x ~ 0.65) or mantissa near 2 after halving."}

function.arguments: {"rationale": "u = fl(1+x) has relative error up to 2^-24 when x is far from 0 (no Sterbenz protection for |x| > 0.5), and the decomposition path (correction, exponent, mantissa) only computes log of u, so the fp32 rounding of 1+x becomes an irreducible relative error ~6e-8 in the output, which at |output| ~ 7.6-11 is 4.5e-7-6.6e-7; stacked with polynomial and log2-split errors this may cross 1e-6. Additionally the mantissa-halving threshold at 1.65 (x in (0.65,1)) coincides with the widest polynomial z range.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "The domain includes the representable value immediately above -1 and every finite FP16 value strictly greater than -1; the tolerance abs(actual[i]-log(1+x[i])) <= 1e-6 is fixed for the entire legal domain."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract explicitly includes values immediately above -1 (output ~ -7.6 to -11) and all x in (-1,0.5), and requires the 1e-6 absolute bound everywhere; the kernel computes log(fl(1+x)) rather than log(1+x), which is only acceptable if within that bound.", "statement": "For x just above -1 (e.g. the FP16 value immediately above -1, or x in (-1,-0.5) generally), the single FP32 rounding of u = fl(1+x) is not fully compensated by the correction term, causing error beyond 1e-6 at the most negative legal outputs."}
